To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MAbs TA3 and TB6 reacted exclusively with T cells in the thymus, and that MAbs TA1, TC4, and TB1 reacted with T cells from different organs.
the MAbs TA3 and TC4 identified a specific antigen restricted only to thymocytes and to some mature T cells.
we have identified a specific antigen restricted only to thymus T cells and different markers belonging in the mature T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of chicken thymocyte-specific antigen and with its distribution in normal tissues, MD cell lines, and in MD tumoral tissues.
the identification of antigens expressed in normal and neoplastic T cells.
the characterization of the T cell population in chicken and the possible use of these antigens for immunotherapeutic purposes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MAbs described are useful for identifying T lymphocytes and for characterizing the T-cell population from normal and tumoral tissues.
these MAbs recognize antigens expressed in normal and neoplastic T cells.
the MAbs TA3 and TB1 recognize a T cell-specific thymocyte antigen, whereas the MAbs TB6, TC4, and TAI recognize antigens expressed by mature T cells and also by MD cell lines and tumor cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MAbs described in this paper could be used to identify T cells and MD tumoral tissues in the chicken.
we have identified two different T-cell populations, a mature one and a less mature one, in the thymus.
the MAbs TA3 and TA1 identify the T cell antigen receptor and the MAbs TB1 and TB6 the T cell receptor-associated molecules.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MAbs obtained are useful to study the differentiation of T cells and the expression of their antigens in normal and MD tissues.
MAbs against chicken thymocyte antigens can be used to identify T cells in different organs and tissues.
the use of monoclonal antibodies is a very powerful tool in the identification of specific antigens in chicken.
